Here's a list of all the things wrong with what you said.

A drone small enough to be launched from the back of a vehicle on the side of the road is going to have a very short flight radius, a couple of miles maximum, and will have little to no payload capability. Furthermore, its only going to have a simple short wave radio transceiver on it for direct line of sight (LOS) control by the person who launched it (think an RC plane), because long wave transceivers or satellite antennas and their requisite larger power supplies will be too big and heavy for a small drone. So there's no feasible way for someone not in the immediate area to be controlling it, unless they set up a relay network of short range radios spanning the entire country.

Large drones either require a runway to take off, or are VTOL which limits their operating range, both distance and altitude. To launch a converted fighter jet using a desert highway as an airstrip will require a lot more than just two guys and a truck. You'll need to section at least a mile or two of the road and have people manning the barricades cause people will just drive around it if nobody is there to stop them.

You'll need some way of securely transporting the aircraft and its payloads there, either putting it on the back of an oversized trailer, which is not sneaky at all, or removing the wings and putting it in a shipping container so you can use a regular semi truck, which is more inconspicuous but will require on-site technicians and specialized machinery to reattach the wings once you're there.

You'll also need a fuel truck because you can't transport a plane loaded with fuel. Aviation fuel, also called Avgas, is very hazardous due to its high octane (100 to 120 is the norm). Avgas is also still leaded because the synthetic fuel additives that were created to replace lead in fuel don't work at altitude, so not only is it begging to start an inferno, but its highly toxic as well.

Speaking of fuel, fighter aircraft don't have very large fuel tanks. Their focus is speed and maneuverability, not range. Most fighter aircraft have a maximum range of a few hundred miles or so, an extra hundred or so with some under-wing fuel pods, but then those pods are taking up anchor points for weapon or surveillance payloads, decreasing the drone's capability.
